executiveSummary: Enforcement of the EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency duties began this week, requiring clear deepfake disclosures and machine-readable marking for synthetic audio, image, video, and text distributed in the EU. This creates immediate compliance and operational impacts for providers and deployers handling AI-generated and manipulated media. Source In the United States, gaps in state-level election deepfake rules persist during an active election period, increasing the risk of voter deception and uneven platform and campaign responses. View Article Financial harm from AI-enabled fraud remains significant. The FBI's latest IC3 report logged 22,364 AI-related complaints and approximately $893 million in adjusted losses, including voice cloning and BEC schemes, while a Hong Kong victim reportedly lost $1.27 million to WhatsApp voice-note impersonation of a family member. Supporting Report View Article Defensive momentum continued with new watermarking research, expanded provenance tooling from major providers, and NIST-led forensics benchmarking initiatives-developments that can strengthen authenticity workflows but require integration and policy alignment to blunt near-term threats.
